event_name: WTI closes at 2016 low ($26.21)
description: Lowest close of 2016 in the dataset, after oversupply pushed prices down from about $37 in early January.

event_name: OPEC agrees first output cut since 2008
description: Agreement in Vienna to cut production; a deal with non-OPEC producers followed on 10 Dec. WTI closed +9.3% on the day (dataset).

event_name: US announces withdrawal from Iran nuclear deal
description: Re-imposition of US sanctions on Iranian oil exports followed in November 2018.
source_name: U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control

event_name: WTI peaks at $76.41 then falls 44% by 24 Dec
description: Peak close of 2018 (dataset); fell to $42.53 on 2018-12-24. Q4 2018 sell-off linked to oversupply worries and a weaker growth outlook - confirm drivers with a source.

event_name: Attack on Saudi Abqaiq and Khurais facilities
description: Temporarily cut about half of Saudi output. WTI +14.7% on the first trading day (16 Sep; dataset).

event_name: OPEC+ talks collapse; Saudi Arabia starts a price war
description: Talks failed on 6 March; Saudi Arabia then announced deep price discounts and higher output. WTI -24.6% on 9 Mar (dataset).

event_name: WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic
description: Lockdowns collapse fuel demand. WTI fell from $34.36 (10 Mar) to $26.95 four sessions later (dataset).

event_name: OPEC+ agrees record 9.7 mb/d cut
description: Record coordinated cut, but demand losses were larger; WTI kept falling (-19.7% over the next four sessions; dataset). Shows that an event does not always move prices the way headlines suggest.

event_name: WTI May contract settles at -$37.63
description: Storage constraints and an expiring contract; the only negative close in the dataset. Percentage returns are undefined here - handled with the abs-change and log-return guards.

event_name: Positive COVID-19 vaccine efficacy results announced
description: Pfizer-BioNTech interim results; WTI +8.5% on the day (dataset).

event_name: OPEC+ agrees to raise output gradually after a standoff
description: Agreement to add about 400k b/d per month from August 2021, resolving a dispute with the UAE.

event_name: US-led coordinated release of strategic reserves
description: US announced a 50-million-barrel SPR release together with China, India, Japan, South Korea and the UK. WTI fell from $78.50 to $66.18 over the next four sessions (dataset), also reflecting Omicron news on 26 Nov.

event_name: Russia invades Ukraine
description: WTI rose from $92.10 (23 Feb) to $110.60 four sessions later (dataset).

event_name: US bans Russian oil imports; WTI closes at 2022 high
description: Close of $123.70 is the 2022 high and the highest close in the dataset; prices fell 13.7% over the next four sessions.

event_name: Fed starts its rate-hiking cycle
description: First hike (+25bp) since 2018; the policy rate reached 5.25-5.50% by July 2023.

event_name: US announces 180M-barrel SPR release
description: Release spread over six months; WTI -7.0% on the day (dataset).

event_name: ECB raises rates for the first time in 11 years
description: +50bp, ending the negative deposit-rate era.

event_name: OPEC+ agrees 2 mb/d production cut
description: WTI +1.4% on the day (dataset).

event_name: EU embargo on Russian seaborne crude and G7 price cap start
description: G7 price cap of $60 per barrel on Russian crude.

event_name: OPEC+ announces surprise voluntary cuts
description: About 1.16 mb/d of additional voluntary cuts. WTI +6.3% on the first trading day (3 Apr; dataset).

event_name: Saudi Arabia announces extra 1 mb/d voluntary cut
description: Starting July 2023; later extended several times.

event_name: Fed makes the final hike of the cycle
description: Policy rate raised to 5.25-5.50%; held until the first cut in September 2024.

event_name: Hamas attacks Israel; Gaza war begins
description: WTI +4.3% on the first trading day (9 Oct; dataset).

event_name: Iran launches drones and missiles at Israel
description: Muted reaction: WTI -0.3% on the first trading day (15 Apr; dataset).

event_name: ECB cuts rates for the first time in the cycle
description: Deposit facility rate: Reduced to 3.75%; Marginal lending facility rate: Reduced to 4.50%; Main refinancing operations rate: Reduced to 4.25%.

event_name: Fed starts cutting rates (-50bp)
description: Bringing the target range down to 4.75%–5.00%. This marked the central bank's first rate reduction since March 2020, ending a 14-month hold at a two-decade peak of 5.25%–5.50%

event_name: US announces broad tariffs; OPEC+ accelerates output increases
description: Tariff announcement on 2 Apr, then an OPEC+ decision on 3 Apr to raise output faster than planned. WTI fell from $71.71 (2 Apr) to $59.58 (8 Apr) (dataset).

event_name: Israel strikes Iran; 12-day war begins
description: WTI +7.3% on 13 Jun. US struck Iranian nuclear sites on 22 Jun and a ceasefire followed on 24 Jun; WTI fell to $64.37 by 24 Jun (dataset).

event_name: OPEC+ agrees to pause output increases in Q1 2026
description: Reported around 1 Dec 2025 - confirm the meeting date.

event_name: WTI closes at 2025 low ($55.27)
description: Followed by a 2026 low of $55.99 on 7 Jan, just before the rally.

event_name: Military action in the Middle East; de facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz
description: Most commercial shipping stopped. First trading day was 2 Mar: WTI +6.3%, and $90.90 four sessions later vs $67.02 on 27 Feb (dataset). Brent had already risen from about $61 to about $72 in Jan-Feb on conflict fears (EIA).

event_name: Iraq, Saudi Arabia and the UAE shut in oil production
description: Production shut-ins in March plus attacks on energy infrastructure (EIA).

event_name: Brent surpasses $100 per barrel
description: WTI closed at $95.73 (dataset). Disrupted Middle East exports hit diesel and jet fuel hardest (EIA).

event_name: Q1 ends: Brent near $118; Brent-WTI spread widens to about $25
description: EIA spot-price basis; the futures-based spread from this dataset will differ. WTI lagged because of strong US inventories and planned SPR releases (EIA).

event_name: WTI closes at 2026 high of $112.95
description: Both benchmarks peaked in early April; Chase quotes year-to-date highs of $114.58 (WTI) and $138.21 (Brent); the Brent figure is far above the highest Brent futures close in the dataset ($118.35 on 31 Mar), so it is probably a spot basis.

event_name: Early-summer pullback on softer demand and a stronger dollar
description: Softer demand from China and Europe, a stronger dollar and higher borrowing costs eased prices; WTI averaged $81.8 in June vs $98.5 in May (dataset).

event_name: OPEC+ signals modest monthly output increases (about 188k b/d)
description: Conflict-related disruptions kept actual production and exports below quotas (Chase).

event_name: Q3 ends: WTI futures $90.42, Brent futures $103.53
description: Futures closes on 30 Sep (dataset). Chase quotes higher end-September levels (WTI $96.16, Brent $113.96) that match no September close in the dataset - probably a spot price basis, so use as context only. US headline CPI rose from 2.4% in January to 3.4% in August (Chase; the FRED-based series in this project agrees).

event_name: IEA warns of market constraints; Saudi officials say Aramco facilities attacked
description: Based on the article headline only (the page could not be retrieved) - read the article and confirm details. WTI +1.0% on the day and $101.79 four sessions later (dataset).

event_name: Brent settles at $116.72 (highest since end-April); WTI $103.27
description: Driven by fears of escalating conflict in West Asia (The Star, 26 Oct 2026).
